History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
28-year-old woman with no significant prior headache history presents with a 4-hour, sudden-onset, left-sided headache accompanied by visual disturbance, dizziness, nausea, and vomiting; clinical impression is probable acute migraine, medication trial initiated with same-day in-person review arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden severe headache beginning this morning (~4 hours prior to call).  
• Character: Left-sided pain, “really painful,” rated 6/10 versus prior kidney-stone pain.  
• Associated symptoms: Blurred vision with zig-zag lines, dizziness, photophobia to screens, nausea, 2 episodes of vomiting.  
• Exacerbating factors: Standing/movement worsens symptoms; head kept still for relief.  
• Attempted treatment: Paracetamol taken ~3 hours earlier—no relief.  
• No focal weakness, gait disturbance, or other focal neurological deficits.  
• Denies previous similar headaches.  
• Review of systems limited to above; no other systems issues reported.

Past Medical History:
• History of kidney stones (no current issues).  
• No other chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• None regularly.  
• Paracetamol – dose/route/frequency not documented (single self-administered dose today).

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Not discussed: smoking, alcohol, recreational drugs, occupation, living situation.

Family History:
• Mother: migraines, hypothyroidism.  
• No other relevant familial conditions reported.

Physical Examination:
(No examination performed during teleconsultation; vitals not available.)

Investigations:
• None obtained during this encounter.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute unilateral headache with visual aura, nausea/vomiting – likely migraine.
  • Educated patient on migraine features and typical course.  
  • Recommended over-the-counter ibuprofen plus anti-emetic combination (specific agents/doses not documented).  
  • Advised drinking sugary, carbonated beverage (e.g., Coca-Cola) for symptomatic relief and hydration.  
  • Discussed response timeframe (30–40 min) and possible duration (4–72 h).  
  • Safety-net advice: seek urgent assessment (A&E) if pain escalates, neurological deficits develop, or no improvement with medication.

Issue 2: Need for in-person neurologic assessment.
  • Same-day appointment arranged for full neurological examination.  
  • If symptoms resolve before appointment, patient may cancel.

General plan items:
  • Encourage rest in dark, quiet room; minimize screen exposure.  
  • Confirm low pregnancy likelihood; no further action.  
  • Provide contact details for interim concerns.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: vital signs, full physical exam, comprehensive medication reconciliation, detailed social history.  
• No internal transcript conflicts identified.  
• Transcript quality: clear; minor connectivity interruptions but did not affect clinical content.
